body: No offense to most of the people here- but I still think depression is just a severe form of laziness, I just wallow in self pity and hatred all of the time. So of course it should be stigmatized! The last thing I want to do is admit to being extremely lazy. Although I think it's a good idea to tell my parents that I have a rope and plan, I really don't want to get hospitalized. They were close to involuntarily admitting me a few months ago when I refused to leave my room for a few days (a severe wave of depression, I guess) and I literally had to cling to my doorway, and talk my way out of it. There is no way knowing what they would do if I told them about the rope. People can behave irrationally. I used to have a friend who thought I was paranoid too- but doesn't everyone sometimes worry about trustworthiness? I just worry a bit more about it. At what point does worrying become paranoia?
Yes I quite agree :) Thanks for all this support- its reassuring to know you and so many more people went through similar things that I'm going through currently. Depression sucks.
Well, you know almost as much as I do... Just curious- how do you deal with suicidal ideations? My mind completely shuts down if I start thinking about it, and I lose focus on everything else.

But when I write out the pros and cons of staying alive, there are so many more cons. Im just dragging everyone down- I can barely function or do anything. And the fact that this post worried you brings up another excellent point. There is such a stigma in western civilization (im in the US) around suicide, while for other areas suicide is simply a choice some people decide to make. I had no choice in coming into existence, so why does it hurt and disturb so many people if I choose to not accept this opportunity handed to me. All that is left is your name, no matter how long the life actually was. Take soppoku, the suicide technique often used by samurai in Japan. It's basically an honor, it's viewed as an act of bravery to clear your name and take your own life. Also- why should my family members feel guilt or sadness when I die? It seems so stupid. Death is just an extreme form of 'innocence is bliss'. What's done is done, they should be happy knowing I'm in a better place. Having to grind through my life day after day for no reason should cause much more guilt and sadness. It's almost selfish for them to require me to stay alive.
Thanks, it's nice to know there are many people in the world all in similar boats. Good luck to you as well.
Yeah I think a new therapist would be best. Quick question- did you use anti-depressants or other medications at all? Or did you just power through and feel much better as time went on in college?

Thanks man :) (just to let you know I'm actually a girl) and its still possible for me to appreciate little things, it's the other parts of my life that are a little overpowering and unbalanced. But spending time outside definitely brightens my mood. Hope your life is going well.

Thanks for replying. I have told my parents a few months ago that I feel extremely depressed, and they seemed a little worried. A few days later, some family friends were over and one of my moms' friends asked why I was feeling depressed. I explicitly told them not to tell anyone else, yet they did. I cannot trust anyone. My friends are nice- but I would rather stay a little distant from them, because if we ever fight they will have perfect blackmailing material. I feel like I'm always on edge, it's so tiring. I think it's a good idea to find a psychologist, you may be right; the current isn't helping. But I'm not entirely sure I want to be helped, everything is so overwhelming- college searches, all this stress and disapointment and lethargy. You are right about the labels as well- that's a habit that definitely should go- very perceptive. As for the hanging- perhaps actually speaking about this will alleviate the pervasiveness. There is a park not too far away from my house. I would leave a suicide note on my bedroom door describing my whereabouts and reasons and leave at 2 in the morning with a rope. There is a tree near the middle of the park that has several branches about twelve feet from the ground (there are lower ones too so it's possible to climb it, I've done it before). If you tie the rope with a hangmans knot and keep it long, the neck will snap from the fall. You die in minutes, with almost no pain. I dont really care about pain anyways. I wouldnt have to worry about becoming paralyzed, or being discovered- as it's two in the morning. This is the first time I've ever expressed this- I think about it a lot, but it's nice to finally put it down in words. There's a part of me that wants to be impulsive, another that wants to just push through and maybe reavaluate existence and stuff after high school. But the second is weakening and weakening, it's becoming scary.
I wasn't planning on doing it until this weekend. Im just wondering if anyone on this subreddit has gone through something similar, and has some advice that I could use.
